subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser-specific URL/domain/path denylist or fold this into a broader egress and SSRF policy design?
rationale: The request would create an operator-facing browser navigation security boundary and public config surface, and the open related items show competing scopes that automation should not choose.

options.title: Design Browser Policy First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define denylist, warnlist, redirect, proxy, default-list, and docs semantics for browser navigation.

options.title: Fold Into Generic Egress Policy
options.body: Make the broader egress-policy issue canonical if maintainers want one domain policy across browser navigation, web_fetch, web_search, and plugin/provider HTTP paths.

options.title: Reject Browser Denylist Surface
options.body: Close the request and document existing hostname allowlist/private-network controls if bot-blocked public domains should remain outside OpenClaw config.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define denylist, warnlist, redirect, proxy, default-list, and docs semantics for browser navigation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest history signal across browser SSRF defaults and navigation policy hardening.
